subject: Demo follow-up + proposed pilot (Lakemont) — scope, success criteria, and kickoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@lakemontventures.com>, Ben Holt <ben.holt@lakemontventures.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo follow-up + proposed pilot (Lakemont) — scope, success criteria, and kickoff

Hi Alyssa / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Quick recap and a proposed pilot we can start as soon as we have your sign-off. I kept scope narrow so we can move quickly and produce measurable results for your ML ops and product teams.

What we demoed
- Contextual retrieval + response generation for investor Q&A workflow (demo dataset).
- Integration options: direct API vs. hosted connector + webhook forwarding.
- Observability: per-request latency/cost and token breakdowns in Redwood Console.

Proposed pilot (3-week technical trial + 1-week evaluation) — high level
- Week 0 (prework, 1 week): access, synthetic dataset, SSO test, API keys, basic firewall/IP allowlist.
- Week 1–3 (trial): run live evaluation using a 400-sample prompt set; integrate via API or connector; enable KV prefix caching and benchmarking.
- Week 4 (evaluation): review metrics, acceptance test, and decision brief.

Success criteria (suggested) — we can tweak these together
1) Latency: p50 < 250ms and p95 < 700ms on your median request profile.
2) Quality: >= 92% entity extraction precision on the curated 400-sample prompt set (we'll agree labeling rules).
3) Cost: unit cost estimates consistent with pilot profile (target: <= $0.003/token average, with caching).
4) Reliability: no more than 1 outage longer than 5m during the 3-week run; automated fallbacks enabled.
5) Security: traffic routed from your VPC/region (US-East) and audit logging enabled.

Owners at Redwood
- Karthik Iyer — SE lead (integration and test harness).
- Marissa Cole — Customer Success (scheduling, acceptance criteria, and playbook).
- Jordan Blake — Deal lead / escalation.

Attachments: Lakemont-POC-outline-v1.pdf (detailed day-by-day), lakemont-integration-prework.xlsx (checklist).

Next steps
- If this looks good, confirm kickoff week of May 9 (we're holding May 10/11 for a technical kickoff).
- Share the sample data access path (or confirm we'll use a synthetic set to start).
- I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Karthik + Marissa and your engineering lead.

One last note: we can offer a pilot credit to offset trial API costs if procurement needs it for PO approval — we can reflect that in the MSA/statement of work.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com]
[Attachment: Lakemont-POC-outline-v1.pdf] [Attachment: lakemont-integration-prework.xlsx]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@lakemontventures.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Holt <ben.holt@lakemontventures.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + proposed pilot (Lakemont) — scope, success criteria, and kickoff

Jordan —

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what our product team was hoping for. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Data residency: we need to confirm all processing stays in US-East (we are sensitive to EU/other regions for this dataset).
2) Instrumentation: do you provide an evaluation harness or sample scripts for measuring precision/recall against our label set?
3) Support level: for the three-week run, will we have an SE on-call for integration spikes?
4) Cost: useful to see a ballpark of expected trial consumption and the pilot credit details before we put a PO in.

Ben and I are leaning to kick off May 9 (May 10 technical kickoff fine too). If you can answer the Qs above and send an updated outline with the prework checklist, we can confirm.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Senior Product Manager
Lakemont Ventures
alyssa@lakemontventures.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@lakemontventures.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + proposed pilot (Lakemont) — scope, success criteria, and kickoff

Hi Alyssa — good questions, answered inline below. Quoting your items for clarity.

> 1) Data residency: we need to confirm all processing stays in US-East.
We can pin the trial to US-East and restrict routing; Redwood Private/Dedicated options available if you need customer-managed networking. For this pilot we'll ensure processing and logs remain in the US-East region and provide an audit snapshot at trial end.

> 2) Instrumentation: do you provide an evaluation harness or sample scripts for measuring precision/recall against our label set?
Yes — Karthik will deploy our evaluation harness (python scripts and a small runner) into a shared Drive folder. It will output per-prompt annotations, precision/recall, and token/cost breakdowns. We'll include a sample notebook to reproduce metrics.

> 3) Support level: for the three-week run, will we have an SE on-call for integration spikes?
Karthik will be the SE lead and available during business hours; Marissa will coordinate escalation windows for off-hours. We can add a short weekly sync (15m) to review run metrics.

> 4) Cost: useful to see a ballpark of expected trial consumption and the pilot credit details before we put a PO in.
I'll send a separate note with an estimated consumption table (sample prompts x expected avg tokens x estimated cost) and the pilot credit offer. Briefly: we typically offer a mid-four-figure credit for trials of this size and can reflect that in an SOW/PO line item.

Proposed pre-kickoff checklist (high level)
- Confirm dataset access (or share synthetic set).
- Create a service account and IP allowlist.
- Confirm SSO/Okta test account for at least one user.
- Slack/Zoom channel for real-time debugging.

We updated the POC outline (attached) to include a day-by-day plan and a shortened acceptance checklist. If May 10 works for your engineers, we can do the technical kickoff then; otherwise May 9 works for a kickoff + alignment call.

Karthik — will follow up with the eval harness link and a brief README by EOD tomorrow.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive
[Attachment: Lakemont-POC-outline-v1.pdf]

Jordan / Alyssa —

Appreciate the thorough plan. A couple procurement items from my side:
- We need an estimate for trial-related costs (even if partially credit-backed) for our PO team.
- We will run a quick legal review of your MSA; any chance you can share a redline-friendly copy or a link to the standard MSA?

Also — if results are positive we expect to move to a 6-month reserved capacity evaluation. Would be useful to get a rough SKU/price range for that scenario in the estimate.

Ben Holt
Head of Procurement
Lakemont Ventures
ben.holt@lakemontventures.com

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + proposed pilot (Lakemont) — scope, success criteria, and kickoff

Ben — thanks, and quick answers: 

1) Trial cost estimate: attaching a short table (expected consumption scenarios). For the pilot profile we estimate $4.2k in list API usage; applying a pilot credit of $3k would leave an expected residual of ~$1.2k depending on actual runs. We'll finalize once you confirm the sample prompt volume.

2) MSA: here's the standard MSA link for redlines: https://drive.google.com/redwood_standard_msa_2026. If you want, I can loop in our legal contact to expedite a review.

3) 6-month reserved estimate: included in the attached estimate doc — rough ballpark shows a 30–40% unit cost improvement with reserved capacity; we can deliver a formal quote if you elect to pursue that post-pilot.

Next steps from us
- I'll upload the cost estimate and a DocuSign SOW template to the Drive folder and share the link.
- We will hold May 10 14:00 ET for a technical kickoff; please confirm attendee list (engineer + security/infra contact preferred).

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com]
[Attachments: lakemont-trial-estimate.xlsx, Lakemont-POC-outline-v1.pdf]
